figures.caption: Transimpedance loop gain at maximum gain, by \texttt{stb} through the \texttt{IPRB\_F} probe, over the five process corners. $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$, $C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$, electrode \texttt{randles\_cell} with $R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$, \SI{25}{\celsius}. DC loop gain is \SIrange{76.5}{78.0}{\decibel} and crossover \SIrange{6.3}{6.7}{\kilo\hertz}. The electrode's solution resistance bounds the noise gain at $1 + R_f/R_s$, so the loop closes at \SI{20}{\decibel} per decade rather than the \SI{40}{\decibel} of the earlier bare-capacitor bench (Section~\ref{sss:tia-loop}).

Loop phase for the same five runs. In this convention \SI{0}{\degree} is the instability point, so the phase at crossover is the phase margin directly: \SIrange{61.2}{64.9}{\degree}. Cadence's \texttt{phaseMargin()} returns exactly \SI{180}{\degree} less on this result and is not used here or in Section~\ref{ss:controlamp}.

Closed-loop transimpedance magnitude, five corners, conditions as Figure~\ref{fig:tia-cl-loopgain}. Peaking is \SIrange{1.2}{1.5}{\decibel} at \SI{3.98}{\kilo\hertz} and the \SI{-3}{\decibel} bandwidth \SIrange{7.2}{7.5}{\kilo\hertz}. Both are set by $C_f$; at $C_f = \SI{5}{\pico\farad}$ the same cell peaks \SIrange{3.0}{3.7}{\decibel} with \SIrange{41.7}{46.4}{\degree} of margin.

tables.caption: Transimpedance loop stability by corner. $R_f = \SI{560}{\kilo\ohm}$, $C_f = \SI{22}{\pico\farad}$, electrode \texttt{randles\_cell} with $R_s = \SI{100}{\ohm}$, $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$, $C_{\mathrm{dl}} = \SI{100}{\nano\farad}$, \SI{25}{\celsius}. Phase margin holds \SIrange{61.2}{64.9}{\degree} against a \SI{45}{\degree} floor and a \SI{60}{\degree} target, with \SI{3.7}{\degree} of corner spread. Loop gain is \SIrange{76.5}{78.0}{\decibel} here because $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{1}{\mega\ohm}$; at $R_{\mathrm{ct}} = \SI{10}{\kilo\ohm}$ the electrode shunts the summing node and it falls to \SIrange{41.9}{44.3}{\decibel}, which is the block's binding limit (Section~\ref{sss:tia-loop}). Schematic-level, no extracted parasitics.

Closed-loop transimpedance by corner, same conditions. Transimpedance at \SI{1}{\hertz} is within \SI{0.02}{\percent} of $R_f$, so DC accuracy is set by the feedback resistor --- which is an ideal element in this bench, not the 16-tap string. The peak lies below the \SI{-3}{\decibel} corner, so the quoted bandwidth is usable; that was not true of the bare-capacitor bench this supersedes.
